decision_record.question: Which Python Causal Forest implementation, exact config, and D30 scale plan satisfy ADR-CF-implementation's selection criteria, for T10's local preflight + Kaggle SMOKE/RESOURCE verification (no held-out, no validation, no real-data SMOKE executed yet)?
candidates_compared: econml.dml.CausalForestDML (same package, adds a DML nuisance-residualization pre-stage)
causalml.inference.tree.CausalRandomForestRegressor (Uber, active, honesty lineage unverified against Wager-Athey/GRF)
skgrf.GRFForestCausalRegressor (crflynn, wraps the literal grf C++ core, but low-activity: 34 stars, 79 commits, vendored grf core lagging current CRAN release)
decision_record.selection_rationale: Single-stage: fits directly on (X, T, y) by solving the local moment equation E[(Y - <theta(x),T> - beta(x))(T;1) | X=x]=0 -- theta(x) (treatment effect) and beta(x) (local intercept) are estimated jointly and locally via forest weights. No upfront nuisance-model fit, no cross-fitting stage -- verified directly from the installed source docstring (econml 0.17.0), not assumed from external documentation. This matches the project's existing pattern (T=design-assigned ITT; no covariate-varying propensity model fit anywhere in T07-T09) and avoids introducing a second nuisance-governance mechanism that CausalForestDML's W/nuisance stage would require. Best-maintained option (4.8k stars, active 2026 commits) versus skgrf's low-activity/version-lag risk and causalml's unverified forest-honesty lineage.

not_selected_reason.econml.dml.CausalForestDML: Adds a DML nuisance-residualization pre-stage (separate model_y/model_t fits) this project has no documented need for -- T is design-assigned, not a confounded observational treatment. Would introduce a second, larger nuisance-governance surface alongside X-Learner's OOF mechanism without justification. Retained as documented fallback only if econml.grf.CausalForest fails a later gate.
not_selected_reason.causalml: Forest-based CausalRandomForestRegressor's honesty/sample-splitting semantics are not confirmed equivalent to Wager-Athey GRF from public documentation; the package's own UpliftRandomForestClassifier (a different class in the same package) uses KL-divergence/ED/chi-square splitting and is explicitly not honest/GRF-style -- same-package name-similarity risk the ADR explicitly warns against.
not_selected_reason.skgrf: Small (34 stars, 79 commits), indeterminate recency, vendored grf C++ core reported behind current upstream (2.1.0 vs CRAN 2.6.1) -- highest integration/maintenance risk despite highest literal Wager-Athey fidelity.

decision_record.criterion_choice: mse (package default). Verified from the installed econml 0.17.0 source docstring: 'mse' is the standard local-moment-estimation split rule (the reference GRF gradient-tree objective); 'het' is a distinct, non-default heterogeneity-score approximation. Frozen as the untouched default per CODE PLAN direction -- not selected by a fidelity ranking claim beyond what the source itself documents, and not tuned.
decision_record.inference_false_rationale: This project's frozen uncertainty mechanism is the 500-draw paired arm-stratified validation bootstrap (AGENTS.md frozen foundation; docs/06), applied post hoc to already-computed scores -- estimator-agnostic, and never consumes any estimator's internal per-row analytic/BLB interval. inference=True's Bootstrap-of-Little-Bags machinery has no downstream consumer in this project's established pipeline; disabling it is the smaller, justified final configuration rather than leaving a default-True flag enabled with no user.
decision_record.n_jobs_determinism_finding: Empirically verified during T10 IMPLEMENT (not assumed): with an identical random_state, n_jobs=2 and n_jobs=-1 each produced different predict() output than n_jobs=1 on the same data. n_jobs=1 is required for bit-identical reproducibility and is frozen despite its runtime cost; this is a correctness requirement, not a performance preference.
decision_record.n_estimators_constraint_finding: econml.grf.CausalForest.fit() raises ValueError unless n_estimators is exactly divisible by subforest_size (default 4) -- discovered via direct source-level testing, not documented prominently. n_estimators=100 (package default) satisfies this (100/4=25) and is frozen unchanged across SMOKE/RESOURCE/FULL per CODE PLAN direction (no borrowed R-grf tree count, no per-stage tuning).
decision_record.serialization_finding: Verified via direct pickle round-trip on a synthetic fixture: predictions after pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(model)) match the original exactly (bit-identical), confirming pickle as the serialization/reload mechanism for T10/T11 artifacts.

frozen_config.min_balancedness_tol_semantics_note: Bounds split-size imbalance between a split's two children -- NOT a treatment/control arm-balance mechanism. Arm support is verified separately via honest_leaf_arm_support().

honesty_support_algorithm.role: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, not a pass/fail gate (corrected -- see support_gate_correction below). Reports per-(tree,leaf) treated/control counts.
honesty_support_algorithm.corrected_index_mapping: tree.get_train_test_split_inds() returns indices LOCAL to forest.get_subsample_inds()[i], not global row indices -- verified empirically (max local index < len(subsample)). Global indices are subsample[split_local] / subsample[est_local]. Leaf support is computed from est_global only via tree.apply(X[est_global]), never split_global.
honesty_support_algorithm.diagnostic_evidence: full empirical distribution (min / 1st percentile / median) of min(n_treated, n_control) across all (tree, leaf) pairs, reported but never gating

support_gate_correction.original_gate_removed: 100% of (tree, leaf) pairs reachable at predict() time must have n_treated>=1 AND n_control>=1 -- REMOVED. Verified over-constrained by direct inspection of econml/grf/_base_grf.py: identification is a forest-AGGREGATE property (predict_alpha_and_jac() averages each tree's local moment contribution across all trees; theta(x) = pinv(aggregate_jac(x)) @ aggregate_alpha(x)), not a per-tree-per-leaf requirement. econml itself implements no such per-leaf constraint by default.
support_gate_correction.finding_that_triggered_review: First real-data local SMOKE attempt (200,000 train-only rows, seed 42, frozen config) found 32.7% of 615,156 reachable (tree,leaf) pairs degenerate (missing one arm, almost entirely zero-control) -- all 100/100 trees affected, median n_control per leaf = 1. Mathematically expected under ~85/15 treatment imbalance with an absolute min_samples_leaf=5 floor and unconstrained max_depth: P(all-treated leaf of size L) ~= 0.85^L (~44% at L=5), independent of N. This finding is retained as diagnostic evidence, not relabeled as estimator failure.

new_gate.mechanism: econml.grf.CausalForest.predict_alpha_and_jac(X) returns the aggregate alpha(x)/jac(x) econml itself uses to compute theta(x). Hard gate per query: alpha(x) finite, jac(x) finite, jac(x) has numpy.linalg.matrix_rank(jac(x)) == full parameter dimension (2: theta(T) + intercept beta) using matrix_rank's own default tolerance -- no invented condition-number cutoff -- and the resulting tau(x) prediction is finite.
new_gate.diagnostic_only_evidence: condition-number distribution (min/p50/p95/p99/max) of jac(x) across all queries, reported but never gating

support_gate_correction.local_verification: tests/test_causal_forest_baseline.py: test_aggregate_jacobian_support_passes_on_balanced_fixture, test_aggregate_jacobian_support_passes_despite_per_leaf_degeneracy (reproduces the ~85/15-imbalance per-leaf degeneracy synthetically and confirms the aggregate gate still passes), test_aggregate_jacobian_support_no_invented_condition_number_cutoff -- all passed.
